chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali al-Asadi, known as Ibn Jurada al-Barda'i, narrated to us from Ruqayya bint Ishaq ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all) who said: My father Ishaq narrated to me, saying: My father Musa narrated to me from his father Ja'far, from his father Muhammad, from his father Ali, from his father al-Husayn, from his father the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

A servant's feet will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is asked about four things: about his youth, how he spent it; about his life, how he used it; about his wealth, from where he acquired it and in what he spent it; and about his love for us, the Ahl al-Bayt.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: the People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What are the four things a person is asked about on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Fadail al-Shia*, this hadith establishes the four pillars of individual accountability, uniquely placing love for the Ahl al-Bayt alongside the management of youth, time, and wealth. This inclusion highlights the Shia theological emphasis that spiritual allegiance to the Prophet’s progeny is as critical as ethical stewardship of one’s physical and material resources. The chain of narration through the Imams underscores the continuity of this teaching from Imam Ali to the final Imam.
